name: OWEB Land Acquisition Grants
summary: Grants for buying interests in land from willing sellers, such as fee title or conservation easements, to protect or restore watersheds and native fish and wildlife habitat in Oregon. Land trusts, tribes and local governments can apply.

steps: Site visit hosted for the technical review team
Present the project at a public hearing for fee-simple acquisitions

eligibility.rule: Can hold OWEB-funded interests in land and continue using them for constitutional purposes
Not a state or federal agency

effort.quote: Land acquisition grant applicants are required to consult with OWEB staff before applying for a grant.
Land Acquisition applications received by 5:00 pm on Thursday, October 15, 2026 will be considered for funding at the April 2027 OWEB board meeting
The reviewers participate in a site visit hosted by the grant applicant in coordination with OWEB staff.
Participate in public hearing (fee simple projects only)
Funding decisions will be made by the board at its April 2027 meeting.

eligibility.quote: Eligible Applicants are entities able to hold OWEB-funded interests in land, as long as the entity continues to use the land for the purposes specified in the constitution
state and federal agencies are eligible to hold OWEB-funded property interests, but cannot be applicants

co_finance.quote: Land acquisition grant applicants must demonstrate that they are seeking or have secured an amount of match that is equal to at least 25% of the total amount of funds they are requesting from OWEB, unless otherwise specified by OWEB. after_award.quote: 5 years after actual date of Closing

documents.quote: A map that shows each property proposed for OWEB funding, any match property, and the location relative to the closest town.
An aerial photograph of each property proposed for OWEB funding.
Organizational Financial Documents (upload type: organizational financial documents)
At least two letters of community or partner support.
Preliminary Title Report (upload type: preliminary title report)
A legible copy of recorded documents for the exceptions listed in the preliminary title report.
A copy of the deed that vested title in the party identified in the preliminary title report.

Evidence of the applicant’s conservation mission that includes the acquisition of interests in property for conservation purposes (e.g., applicable section of corporate charter, bylaws, statute, or board resolution). • Non-governmental organizations must submit their bylaws with the application.
The Landowner Acknowledgement form completed and signed by the seller or seller’s representative, for each property interest proposed for OWEB funding.
